```{r}

#| warning: FALSE
#| error: FALSE

#install cmribio from github
#library(pak)
#pak::pkg_install("jmvarberg/cmribio")

library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(ggsci)
library(ggpubr)
library(rstatix)
library(data.table)
library(DT)

#download logo to use for example
logo <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmvarberg/cmribio/main/man/figures/logo.png"
dest <- "logo.png"

download.file(logo, dest)
```

## Results

### Table 1: Summary of Study Design and Cohort

### Tables and Graphs

Include separate sections and chunks used to generate results tables and plots during the analysis.

#### Static and Interactive Tables {#sec-tables}

Here are simple examples of how to make static or interactive tables.

```{r}
#| label: tables

#static table output
mtcars |> 
  knitr::kable()

#interactive table output
mtcars |> 
  cmribio::cmri_datatable()
```


#### Static and Interactive Plots

Here are basic examples of using static and interactive plots.
 
```{r}
#| label: fig-static-plot
#| fig-cap: "Static penguin plot"
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt, color = factor(cyl), text1 = disp, text2=drat, text3 = qsec, text4 = gear, text5 = carb)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  scale_color_bcb() +
  theme_bcb(base_theme = "bw")

#static plot
p + ggtitle("Static Plot Output")
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-interactive-plot
#| fig-cap: "Interactive plot"
library(plotly)
#interactive plot
pp <- p + ggtitle("ggplotly Interactive Output")
ggplotly(pp)
```


You can also modify the size of the plot generated by each chunk like this:

```{r}
#default size
p
```


```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12

p
```

### Embedded files

The function `xfun::embed_file()` and related functions can be used to directly embed results files, like CSVs or Excel files, into the document. It will then be self-contained, so anyone with the report can download the embedded file.

```{r, eval = F}

#showing simple example

#create results data frame
results <- mtcars

#save results to the project results directory
write.csv(mtcars, "./results/mtcars.csv", row.names = F)

#also embed a copy of the results in the HTML report for quick access and sharing with collaborators
xfun::embed_file("./results/mtcars.csv", "./results/mtcars.csv", "Results - mtcars.csv")
```
